ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.40 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method and log the route-deviation with a reminder to the driver; no formal warning (first notification incident). Do not flag the driver account (the only profile entries outstanding are a no-show dispute, not an upheld route deviation within 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat and complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation — no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 trigger, so the case can be ruled on the merits.

Route deviation: the record shows a real, measured off-route stretch at 14:27–14:29 — 1.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.67 km, adding ~1.23 km and reaching up to 874 m from the optimal route [F4]. The overall GPS deviation of +0.3 km [F2] is only the netted residual of a trip whose trace is partly missing, so it does not cancel the measured segment; the billed excess is 2.41 km / $3.40 [F5].

Consent (RD-5 / RD-3): the only rider message about routing is Chat #3 at 14:29 [F10], asking to go via Canning Lane after the off-route segment had already begun; notice or consent after the segment began does not count, so it cannot exempt any part of the 14:27–14:29 segment. The driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS rerouted" [F12] is an explanation given only after the fact — it is not notice in-app or by recorded call before or at the point of deviation, and there is no call recording.

Traffic (RD-4): no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the window [F15], and the only speed-band data is for EU TONG SEN STREET (band 4) and KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD (band 5) [F13][F14] — neither is band 1–2, and neither sits on the replaced part of the recommended route (Cantonment Rd / Lim Teck Kim Rd / Bernam St / Anson Rd / Maxwell Rd / Wallich St / Cecil St). So there is no traffic justification; RD-2 gives a partial refund of the excess distance fare and a recorded driver violation.

Amount: refundable km = deviation − exempt km. No segment is exempt, so refundable km = 1.23 km of extra distance on the measured segment; the trip's own rate is $1.4099/km, giving $1.73. The fare record already bills the excess as $3.40 (2.41 km × $1.4099/km) [F5] (the 2.41 km figure is the stored excess-distance computation, which includes the map-matching residual); per RD-2 the refund is of the excess distance fare as given, so $3.40. This is the whole overcharge and excludes time fare, platform fee and tolls.

Action level: $3.40 is under $10, so the system ruling is final (TH-1, TH-2, C1, consistent with DISP-001's automatic $3.44 deviation refund). The driver's earlier upheld dispute was a no-show, not a route deviation, so RD-6's 90-day repeat-deviation flag does not apply [F18].

Evidence caveat (does not affect the outcome): the GPS trace leaves the last 4 minutes of the trip uncovered [F1], but the discrepancy and the segment are both measured within the covered stretch and the fare is fully recorded [F5][F7], so the refund computation does not depend on the missing portion.

segment_findings.reason: The 14:27–14:29 segment (1.90 km vs 0.67 km optimal, +1.23 km, up to 874 m off route) was driven before any rider routing request: Chat #3 asking to go via Canning Lane came at 14:29, i.e. only after the segment began, and no consent for the segment appears before it [F10]. The driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted [F12] is not notice in-app or by recorded call before or at the point of deviation (RD-5), there is no traffic reason (no incident [F15]; the only speed bands are 4 and 5 on unrelated roads [F13][F14]) (RD-4), and no rider-named road/stop covers it (RD-3). Segment therefore counts as deviation and its 1.23 km of extra distance is refundable (RD-2).

element_findings.element: Notice and consent for the reroute (RD-5: in-app chat or recorded call before/at the point of deviation)
element_findings.reason: No driver notice appears before or at 14:27; the only rider routing message is Chat #3 at 14:29, after the segment began, and the driver's written statement [F12] is a post-trip explanation with no call recording. Late notice/consent does not count.

element_findings.element: Traffic reason for the reroute (RD-4: incident within 300 m/on the route, or speed band 1–2)
element_findings.reason: No traffic incidents recorded on or near the route during the trip window [F15]; the recorded bands are 4 (EU TONG SEN STREET) and 5 (KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD), neither band 1–2 nor on the replaced part of the recommended route.

element_findings.element: Reason the driver took the other way (RD-2 matrix / RD-3): rider-requested route vs driver/other cause
element_findings.reason: No rider request covers the segment before it began and the driver offers only a GPS reroute claim, so the segment is attributable to the driver's own routing, not to a rider-requested route or stop (RD-3 not applicable).

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the GPS sent him that way is an after-the-fact explanation with no in-app notice before or at the point of deviation and no call recording, so it neither satisfies RD-5 notice nor exempts the segment; system records (GPS segment times/distances, absence of any traffic event) override it.
The rider's request to go via Canning Lane was sent at 14:29, after the off-route segment had already begun, so it cannot exempt that segment under RD-5/RD-3 (consent after the fact is not consent).

ruling.evidence_gap: GPS trace stops 4 min 0 s before drop-off [F1]; the uncovered tail is named but is not outcome-relevant because the discrepancy, the off-route segment and the full fare build-up are all recorded.
